mainTopic: Using הערמה to keep an unborn animal from becoming a בכור, רב יהודה's ruling on blemishing a בכור before birth, and which cases the end of the משנה is about
overview: The משנה teaches a strategy (הערמה): before an animal gives birth for the first time, the owner declares that the unborn male will be an עולה, so it never becomes a בכור for the כהן. It then goes through different birth outcomes: a male, a female, a male and a female, two males, two females, and a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס. In the גמרא, רב יהודה rules that one may give a בכור a blemish (מום) before it is born. The גמרא challenges him from the משנה, which seems to allow only an עולה, a stronger holiness. The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks of when the בית המקדש stands, while רב יהודה means today. It also explains why his ruling is still needed: there is no גזרה against it, because blemishing early stops the owner from shearing or working the בכור. Then the גמרא clears up the end of the משנה. The female שלמים case is about the young of a הקדש animal, and the two-males case is about an ordinary mother. The amud ends by quoting the טומטום and אנדרוגינוס line, and the discussion of it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How to consecrate an unborn firstborn ahead of time
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that an owner can declare the unborn male of a first-time mother an עולה, and the unborn female a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: How can one use a strategy regarding the firstborn? If an animal is pregnant with its first offspring, the owner says: 'What is in this animal's womb, if it is male, is an עולה.' If it gives birth to a male, it is offered as an עולה. If he also said 'and if it is female, it is a שלמים,' and it gives birth to a female, it is offered as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens by teaching a legal strategy. The owner gives the unborn animal a holy status before it is born, so it never becomes a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a firstborn male becomes a בכור at birth and goes to the כהן. Because the owner already declared it an עולה while it was in the womb, the עולה status comes first. The newborn is then brought as his own offering instead.

keyTerms.meaning: use a clever legal strategy (הערמה) to get around an obligation
a firstborn male animal, which is holy and given to the כהן
an animal giving birth for the first time
a burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
peace offerings, which are partly eaten by the owners

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic case the whole סוגיא is built on. The גמרא will soon use it to challenge רב יהודה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: How may one use a strategy regarding the firstborn?
phrases.notes: The trick here keeps the animal from becoming a בכור that has to go to the כהן.

phrases.english: An animal giving birth for the first time, while it was pregnant, he says:
"What is in the womb of this one,
if male, is a burnt offering,"
if it gave birth to a male, it is offered as a burnt offering;
"and if female, peace offerings,"
if it gave birth to a female, it is offered as a peace offering.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Declaring an unborn first offspring an עולה (if male) or a שלמים (if female) takes effect, and the newborn is offered accordingly.

steps.title: Twins: a male and a female, or two males
steps.stepSummary: If the animal has a male and a female, each follows its condition. If it has two males, one is an עולה and the other is sold to someone who needs an עולה, and the money stays ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'if male, an עולה; if female, a שלמים,' and it gave birth to a male and a female, the male is offered as an עולה and the female as a שלמים. If it gave birth to two males, one is offered as an עולה, and the second is sold to people who must bring an עולה, and the money from the sale is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with cases where the animal gives birth to two babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a male and a female, each baby simply follows its own condition. With two males, only one is offered by the owner himself. The second is sold to someone who must bring an עולה, and the sale money is ordinary (חולין), not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: people who are obligated to bring a burnt offering
its money, meaning the payment received for it
ordinary, not holy

phrases.english: "If male, a burnt offering,
and if female, peace offerings,"
and it gave birth to a male and a female,
the male is offered as a burnt offering,
and the female is offered as a peace offering.
If it gave birth to two males,
one of them is offered as a burnt offering,
and the second is sold to those obligated to bring a burnt offering,
and its money is non-sacred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the basic declaration to births of two offspring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Male and female: each follows its condition. Two males: one is an עולה, and the other is sold to someone obligated in an עולה, with the money remaining חולין.

steps.title: Two females, or a baby whose gender is unclear
steps.stepSummary: Two females work the same way as two males. For a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says no holiness takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it gave birth to two females, one is offered as a שלמים, and the second is sold to people who must bring a שלמים, and the money is not holy. If it gave birth to a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: holiness does not take effect on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the list of cases: two females, and a baby that is neither clearly male nor clearly female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two females follow the same pattern as two males. For a baby that is neither clearly male nor clearly female, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that no holiness takes effect on it at all. The גמרא will soon look at how far this ruling goes.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal whose gender cannot be seen, because its organs are covered
an animal with both male and female organs
holiness does not take effect

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's main idea: if you declare the unborn animal an עולה before birth, it never becomes a בכור.

phrases.english: If it gave birth to two females,
one of them is offered as a peace offering,
and the second is sold to those obligated to bring a peace offering,
and its money is non-sacred.
If it gave birth to a tumtum or a hermaphrodite,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Sanctity does not take effect on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of birth outcomes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two females: one is a שלמים, and the other is sold to someone obligated in a שלמים, with the money remaining חולין. A טומטום or אנדרוגינוס receives no holiness, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Blemishing a firstborn before it is born
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that one may give a בכור a blemish while it is still in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב יהודה said: It is permitted to put a blemish on a בכור before it comes out into the air of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from רב יהודה. It goes even further than the משנה's strategy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור only becomes holy once it is born. So before birth, there is no holy animal yet, and it is not forbidden to blemish it. Once it is born with a blemish, it cannot be offered on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: to cause a blemish, a physical defect that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
literally 'the air of the world'; being born
permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling lets the owner avoid the בכור's holiness far more completely than the משנה's method does. That is what sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda says:
It is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn
before it comes out into the air of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מוּתָּר לְהַטִּיל מוּם בִּבְכוֹר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may blemish a בכור before it is born, since it is not yet holy.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה only allows an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that the unborn animal can be made an עולה but not a שלמים. So how can רב יהודה allow removing its holiness entirely?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: A person says, 'What is in this animal's womb is an עולה.' An עולה, yes; a שלמים, no. And you say that you can remove its holiness completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's ruling using our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentions making the unborn male an עולה. The גמרא reads this as a limit: only something as holy as an עולה is allowed, not a lighter holiness like שלמים. If even a שלמים is not allowed, how could רב יהודה permit blemishing the animal and taking away its holiness completely?

keyTerms.meaning: yes
no
you remove or cancel
holiness

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה did allow a שלמים, but only for a female. A female is not a בכור anyway. The 'שלמים, no' inference is about the male, the animal that would have become a בכור.

phrases.english: We learned: A person says,
"What is in the womb of this one is a burnt offering":
a burnt offering, yes; a peace offering, no.
And you say
that you can remove it from its sanctity!
phrases.notes: He means blemishing it before birth, as רב יהודה allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן אוֹמֵר אָדָם מַה שֶּׁבְּמֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's ruling using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that one may blemish a בכור before birth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows only an עולה, which is a stricter holiness, and not even a שלמים. So removing the holiness completely by blemishing should certainly be forbidden.

steps.title: רב יהודה is talking about our times, without a בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the משנה's rule applies when the בית המקדש stands. His own ruling is for today, when the animal cannot be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה can say to you: That rule applies when the בית המקדש is standing. When I said my rule, I meant nowadays, when the animal cannot be brought as a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה from the question in step 5. It splits the two rulings into two different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the בית המקדש stands, a בכור can be offered, so you may only give it a stronger holiness, like עולה. Today a בכור cannot be offered at all, and it just waits until it gets a blemish. So giving it a blemish in the womb takes nothing away from the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in a certain case)
When the בית המקדש is standing
Nowadays, after the חורבן
Offering on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב יהודה's ruling is a practical הלכה for today's בכורות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda could say to you:
These words apply
when the Beis HaMikdash is standing;
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule, which only allows giving the unborn animal a stronger holiness.

phrases.english: when I said my rule,
I meant nowadays,
when it is not fit to be offered.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different time periods
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling clashes with the משנה, which only allows a stronger holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the time of the בית המקדש; רב יהודה is about today

steps.title: If it is only for today, why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רב יהודה means only nowadays, isn't his ruling obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he means nowadays, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If a בכור today can never be offered anyway, why would רב יהודה need to teach that you may give it a blemish?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today the animal is only waiting for a blemish so it can be eaten. So permission to give it a blemish before it is born seems too obvious to need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (it seems obvious)

phrases.english: If it is nowadays,
what is there to say? (It is obvious!)

steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב יהודה's ruling once it is limited to nowadays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling that is obvious should not need to be taught

steps.title: We might have made a decree in case most of the head comes out
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed because we might have thought חז"ל made a גזרה. The worry is that the head may already be mostly out when the blemish is given.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: Let us make a גזרה, because perhaps most of its head will come out, and then the person will give it a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב יהודה's ruling is not obvious. Without it, we could have thought it is forbidden because of a גזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once most of the head is out, the animal counts as born and has full בכור holiness. Giving it a blemish then is forbidden. So we might have banned blemishing in the womb at all, in case it happens at that moment. רב יהודה teaches that there is no such גזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken thought the ruling comes to correct)
Let us make a גזרה (a rabbinic safety decree)
Most of its head; at that point it counts as born
A blemish that disqualifies an animal from the מזבח

phrases.english: You might have said: Let us make a decree,
since perhaps most of its head will come out,
phrases.notes: Once most of the head is out, it counts as born and is fully a holy בכור.

phrases.english: and he will then put a blemish on it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is needed to rule out a possible גזרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blemishing in the womb would be banned because of a גזרה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה teaches there is no such גזרה

steps.title: Maybe we really should make that decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not actually make the גזרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is indeed so: we should make the גזרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The worry about the head coming out sounds real, so maybe the גזרה is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said רב יהודה teaches there is no גזרה. Now the גמרא asks why we should not worry. The fear of blemishing an animal that is already born seems like a good reason to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say: indeed so! (Let us make the decree.)

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's decision not to make the גזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry behind the גזרה seems serious enough to justify it

steps.title: Blemishing early is better, so people won't shear or work the בכור
steps.stepSummary: Even so, blemishing it early is better. Otherwise the owner may come to shear the בכור or work with it while waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, this is much better, because otherwise he may come to shear it or work with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we do not make the גזרה. Leaving the animal without a blemish leads to a bigger risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A perfect בכור today must wait, sometimes a long time, until it gets a blemish. During that time the owner might shear it or work with it, which is forbidden. Giving it a blemish early lets it be eaten soon after birth, so that risk goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is much better
Shearing; forbidden with a בכור
Working with the animal; forbidden with a בכור

steps.whatToRemember: Nowadays you may give a בכור a blemish in the womb. There is no גזרה against it, because it prevents the owner from shearing or working the animal.

phrases.english: Even so,
this is much better,
than that he come to shear it or work with it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighs two risks and picks the smaller one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry about the head coming out calls for a גזרה
steps.terutzMaskana: Blemishing early is better because it stops the owner from shearing or working the בכור

steps.title: A female is never a בכור, so why make it a שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. Why would one need to declare a female unborn a שלמים, when a female never has בכור holiness?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says, if it is a female, it is a שלמים. But does a female become holy as a בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the end of the משנה from step 1 and asks a question on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only male firstborns are holy as a בכור. A female from a first-time mother is ordinary anyway. So why does the משנה present calling it a שלמים as part of this case?

keyTerms.meaning: A female animal
שלמים (peace) offerings
The holiness of a firstborn, which applies only to males

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the female is a בכור. The question is exactly that a female never is one.

phrases.english: "If it is a female, it is a peace offering":
phrases.notes: This quotes the end of the משנה from step 1.

phrases.english: Does a female become holy with firstborn holiness?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נְקֵבָה זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים — נְקֵבָה מִי קָא קָדְשָׁה בִּבְכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב יהודה and turns to the end of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The end of the משנה: "if it is a female, it is a שלמים"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A female has no בכור holiness, so this part of the case seems to make no sense

steps.title: The end of the משנה is about the young of a consecrated animal
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה is not about a בכור. It is about the unborn young of an animal that is already הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The end of the משנה comes to teach about an animal of הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the end of the משנה is a different case. It is about an animal that is already holy, not a firstborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother is a holy animal, its young can be holy even if it is female. One example is a חטאת, whose young cannot be offered. So the owner gives the female young a specific holiness, שלמים, before it is born.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה
An animal that is already consecrated (holy)

steps.whatToRemember: The start of the משנה (the male as an עולה) is about a בכור. The end (the female as a שלמים) is about the young of a holy animal.

phrases.english: The latter clause comes to teach about a consecrated animal.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the end of the משנה is a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה is about a firstborn
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of the משנה is about the young of a holy animal, so the female is relevant

steps.title: Why isn't the second male calf holy like its mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of two male calves and asks a question. If the mother is a הקדש animal, the second calf should carry its mother's holiness, so its money should not be חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if it gave birth to two males, one is offered as an עולה and the other is sold, and its money is ordinary. The Sages ask: if this is a consecrated animal, fine, the one he set aside as an עולה is an עולה. But the other calf should keep its mother's holiness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, two male calves, and asks a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 we learned that the end of the משנה is about the unborn young of an animal that is already הקדש. If so, every calf born to that mother is holy because of the mother. So how can the משנה say that the money for the second calf is חולין (ordinary)?

keyTerms.meaning: Two males (two male calves born together)
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
An animal that already belongs to the בית המקדש (it is holy)
The holiness of its mother, which passes to her young

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of holiness. One calf is holy because he called it an עולה. The question is about the other calf, which might be holy only because its mother is holy.

phrases.english: If it gave birth to two males, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: one is offered as an עולה, and the other is sold to someone who needs an עולה, and the money is ordinary.

phrases.english: They say: If it is a consecrated animal,
then the one he consecrated as a burnt offering,
let it be a burnt offering, fine;
but the other should have the holiness of its mother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It uses step 12's reading (the end of the משנה is about a הקדש mother) and tests that reading against the next case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the money for the second male calf is חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the mother is הקדש, every calf she bears gets her holiness. So the second calf cannot be ordinary, and its money cannot be חולין.

steps.title: This last part is about an ordinary mother animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the very end of the משנה switches to a חולין (ordinary) animal, so the second calf has no holiness from its mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part of the משנה is about an ordinary animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying that this last part of the משנה is about an ordinary mother animal, not a holy one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother is חולין, the calves get no holiness from their mother, unlike the case in step 13. Their holiness comes only from the owner's declaration, so nothing forces the money for the second calf to be holy. That is why the משנה can say its money is ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
Now we have come to (the text has moved to a new case)
An ordinary animal that is not holy

steps.whatToRemember: The end of the משנה moves between cases. The female שלמים case is about a הקדש mother (step 12). The two-males case is about a חולין mother.

phrases.english: In the last part, we have come to an ordinary animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question of step 13 by changing which case this part of the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-setting the case: this part of the משנה is about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the whole end of the משנה was about a הקדש mother, so the second calf should be holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two-males case is about a חולין mother. The second calf has no holiness from its mother, so its money is ordinary.

steps.title: Quoting the next case: a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a mother who gives birth to a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס, to set up the next discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if it gave birth to a טומטום or an אנדרוגינוס, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that these calves do not become holy. The גמרא brings up this line to look closely at how far that ruling goes.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose gender cannot be seen, because it is covered
An animal with both male and female features

phrases.english: If it gave birth to a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that these do not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The two-males discussion is finished. This step opens the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a טומטום or אנדרוגינוס born to the animal does not become holy.
